name: Mehdi Karimi (synthetic)

facts.label: pick orders for dispatching
facts.story: Picks tyre orders in a distribution warehouse and suggested grouping the pick lists by aisle during the winter peak.

facts.label: pallets loading
facts.story: Loads trucks and pallets with a reach truck and checks with the drivers what is on the truck.

facts.label: stack goods
facts.story: Stacks and wraps pallets safely and shows new temporary workers how it is done.

facts.label: monitor stock level
facts.story: Counts his aisle on Fridays from the cycle count list and reports differences to the shift lead before changing anything.

facts.label: use barcode scanning equipment
facts.story: Works with a handheld scanner connected to the warehouse system.

answers.recent_work: For the last year and a half I've worked in a distribution warehouse for car tyres, picking orders and loading trucks, mostly with a reach truck. Before that I was a baker for six years, on night shifts, so I'm used to early starts and heavy lifting. I'm a single dad with a daughter in school, and I like that picking orders and driving the reach truck comes with fixed hours.
answers.example: In October we got double the normal volume of winter tyres. I noticed the pick lists were sending people across the whole warehouse for single tyres, so I suggested grouping orders by aisle in the handheld scanner and I tried it for a week on my own shift. We got the evening orders out before the trucks left, which hadn't happened in two weeks.
answers.tools: Reach truck and pallet jack, with the forklift licence. A handheld barcode scanner connected to the warehouse system. Stretch wrap machine and strapping. I also check stock counts with the cycle count list on Fridays.
answers.people: I'm on a shift of twelve. The shift lead gives us the order list and I work mostly with another picker and the truck loader. I help the new temp workers on my aisle, and show them the system and safe stacking. Drivers get their pallets from me, so I talk with them about what's on the truck.
answers.beyond: The bakery taught me time planning and hygiene rules. I also have a driving licence for vans and I did a safety course on working at heights last year.
answers.open_floor: I take a few minutes each shift to tidy my aisle so the next shift starts clean. People notice and copy it.
answers.looking_for: More hours in logistics, maybe team lead later, or a warehouse job with a bigger system to learn. English at work; I can manage everyday Finnish, so I would list both. Day shift is better. I can start after one month's notice.

probes: The grouping idea: I took the evening's list and sorted it by aisle on a sheet first to test it, and saw we'd save about a third of the walking. Then the shift lead asked IT to switch it on for the scanners.
For cycle counts I go to my assigned aisle, scan each location, count the pallets, and enter the number. If it differs from the system, I count again and tell the shift lead before changing anything.
